extracted.intended_audience: former USPTO patent examiners seeking registration, practitioners/attorneys representing them, USPTO/OED decisionmakers
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluative standards governing waiver of the USPTO registration examination for former patent examiners (37 C.F.R. § 11.7(d)(2)) and related standards for suspending regulations (37 C.F.R. § 11.3). Covers required service, performance ratings, warnings, evidentiary considerations, and the Director's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver eligibility under 37 C.F.R. § 11.7(d)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may waive the registration examination for a former patent examiner who, by July 26, 2004, had actively served at least four years in the patent examining corps and was serving at the time of separation, provided that (1) the former examiner was rated at least fully successful in each quality performance element of his or her performance plan for the last two complete fiscal years as a patent examiner in the Office; and (2) was not under an oral or written warning regarding the quality performance elements at the time of separation. (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.7(d)(2)(i)-(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver is contingent on meeting all regulatory elements: qualifying period of service, the 'fully successful' ratings in every quality element for the last two complete fiscal years, and absence of any oral/written warning re: quality elements at separation. Failure on any element supports denial of waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver is discretionary, not automatic
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation makes waiver discretionary: the OED Director 'may' waive the examination rather than must or shall; waiver is not automatic even if some criteria are met (see 69 Fed. Reg. 35,428, 35,438 (June 24, 2004)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not expect automatic relief simply by meeting some criteria; the Director examines the record and exercises discretion (courts have upheld refusals to waive: Leeds v. Mosbacher). Arguments that single errors or non-life-or-death context excuse failing performance ratings are not the regulatory standard for waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for suspension/waiver of regulations (37 C.F.R. § 11.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any requirement of Part 11 that is not a statutory requirement may be suspended or waived by the USPTO Director (or designee) in an 'extraordinary situation, when justice requires.' (37 C.F.R. § 11.3(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'extraordinary situation' standard is very high. Applicants who previously might have sought waiver under deleted § 11.7(d)(2)(iv) must now show extraordinary circumstances under § 11.3; ordinary performance problems, admissions of error, or lack of explanation typically will not meet this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to demonstrate necessary qualifications absent waiver (statutory/regulatory authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. § 11.7(a)(2), the Director may require representatives to show they possess the legal, scientific, and technical qualifications necessary to render valuable service; an applicant must demonstrate necessary legal and competence qualifications by taking and passing the registration examination unless the requirement is waived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If waiver is denied, the applicant bears the obligation to take and pass the registration examination to establish qualifications. The Director's judgment centers on whether the record shows equivalent competence to passing the exam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which performance records are controlling (last two complete fiscal years)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director's analysis is limited by the regulation to the quality element ratings from the applicant's last two complete performance plans (i.e., the last two complete fiscal years as an examiner) when determining eligibility under § 11.7(d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the regulatory test focuses on ratings in the last two complete fiscal years, the Director may consider other matters in the record (e.g., oral warnings, earlier performance trends) to put deficiencies in context and to determine whether the applicant possesses required qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of oral or written warnings regarding quality performance
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who was under an oral or written warning regarding the quality performance elements at the time of separation is disqualified from waiver under § 11.7(d)(2)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral warnings in the record (e.g., issued because of an unacceptable error rate) may be considered dispositive evidence that the applicant was not meeting quality standards and thus counsel denial of waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance/error rate threshold as a basis for marginal/unacceptable rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance ratings in the 'patentability' quality element turn on measured error rates; the decision notes that an oral warning was issued when an examiner's error rate was 18% (unacceptable) and that to achieve at least a marginal rating an error rate must not exceed a specified maximum (the decision references 'requiring an error rate not to exceed 7%').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High error rates (examples in the record: 18%, 20%) justify marginal/unacceptable patentability ratings. An applicant's admission of exceeding the maximum error rate undermines claims for waiver. The Director will not disregard such error-rate-based ratings merely because the absolute number of allowances was low.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance of averages or docket size when evaluating error rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments that the examiner's low number of allowances or unique docket make error rates unreliable do not automatically invalidate performance-based ratings; the Director may examine averages for context but will not disregard an examiner's error rate just because the number of allowances was low.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant should provide persuasive record evidence showing why raw error-rate metrics are misleading; without such evidence, the Director may hold applicants to the same error-rate standards as peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to show cure of prior deficiencies / continuing competence
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant seeking waiver must demonstrate satisfactory patent prosecution skills following any marginal rating or prior deficiencies; temporary improvement that later deteriorates does not show cure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director looks for consistent, sustained competence. Variable performance (improvement followed by regression) and failure to correct deficiencies weigh against waiver. Admissions of not contesting prior ratings hurt the petitioner's case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirement for petitions for review
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to the USPTO Director from the OED Director's final decision under 37 C.F.R. § 11.2(d) must be accompanied by the appropriate fee (see 37 C.F.R. § 1.21(a)(5)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to follow procedural fee requirements can affect the consideration of a petition for review; petitions should comply with fee and filing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deleted 'good cause' waiver route; use § 11.3 instead
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 11.7(d)(2)(iv), which provided for waiver upon showing 'good cause,' was deleted in the Final Rule effective July 26, 2004; individuals who believe requirements should be waived must rely on § 11.3 (extraordinary situation) rather than a prior 'good cause' provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants cannot rely on the deleted good-cause provision; they must frame any equitable arguments under the far more demanding § 11.3 standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible scope of the OED Director's inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the regulation focuses the eligibility inquiry on the last two complete performance plans, the Director may consider all matters in the administrative record that bear on whether the applicant possesses the necessary qualifications to render valuable service in preparation and prosecution of patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant should anticipate that the Director will review both formal ratings and contextual evidence (warnings, error rates, patterns over time) rather than a narrow checklist; silence or admissions in the record about deficient performance are damaging.
